fields.place: Navadvīpa (Śrīhaṭiyā or Dakṣiṇapāḍā), his house where Nityānanda first stayed; earlier Bahirkhaṇḍa near Tārakeśvar; later Purī
fields.notes:
A branch of Lord Caitanya: «the two Lords stayed hidden in his house» (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 10.39). Son of the astrologer Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa Sarvajña, who cast the Lord's horoscope; brother of Bhagavān Adhikārī Sārvabhauma; lame. Nityānanda stayed in his house when He came to Navadvīpa and the Lord found Him there; Advaita hid there on the day of the Mahāprakāśa (Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna; Bhakti-ratnākara 12.2422-2423).

In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Hariṇī (Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna).

fields.name: Nandana (brother of Viṣṇudāsa and Gaṅgādāsa)
fields.notes: Of Nityānanda's branch: «Viṣṇudāsa, Nandana, Gaṅgādāsa — three brothers, in whose house Nityānanda had stayed before» (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 11.43; Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna, «Nandana» 2); the record's text: son of Caturbhuja Paṇḍita of Navadvīpa. The Abhidhāna keeps him apart from Nandana Ācārya (#970), the son of Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa, in whose house the Lord and Nityānanda met; the record's text took them as one (07-11-2026).

fields.place: Navadvīpa; Mādhāi's samādhi at Mādhāi-tolā, Ākāihāṭ (near Katwa)
fields.notes:
Two brāhmaṇa cousins of Navadvīpa, kotwāls under the Muslim ruler and great sinners, delivered by Nityānanda and the Lord: «witnesses to His name Patita-pāvana» (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 10.120; Caitanya-bhāgavata Madhya 13). Grandfather Śubhānanda Rāya; Jagāi son of Raghunātha Rāya, Mādhāi of Janārdana Rāya (Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna). Mādhāi was later called Mādhāi Brahmacārī.

In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Jaya and Vijaya, the door-keepers of Vaikuṇṭha (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 145).

fields.place: A village on the Padmā in East Bengal (Rāmapura: Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna); then Vārāṇasī
fields.notes: A brāhmaṇa of East Bengal, taught by the Lord in a dream and in person, sent by Him to Vārāṇasī; there the Lord ate in his house, and by his efforts the Māyāvādī sannyāsīs of Kāśī were delivered (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 10.152-153, 16.10-11, Madhya 17.83-100; Caitanya-bhāgavata Ādi 14). Father of Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī.

Branch of Śrī Caitanya: «Bhāgavatācārya, Ṭhākura Sāraṅgadāsa» (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 10.113). Lived under a bakula tree in Navadvīpa and crossed the Gaṅgā every evening for the Lord's kīrtana. On the Lord's order he gave dīkṣā to the first person he met: a dead boy floating on the Gaṅgā, who came back to life and became Ṭhākura Murāri (not Murāri Gupta). The Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna has two entries, Sāraṅgadāsa Ṭhākura and Sāraṅgadeva, «probably the same person».

In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Nāndīmukhī (some say Prahlāda) (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 172).

The record «Sharanga Murāri Ṭhākura» #1866 was the same person and was joined to this one (07-11-2026).

First named Pradyumna Brahmacārī; the Lord named him Nṛsiṁhānanda for his devotion to his Deity of Nṛsiṁha (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 10.55-56). He built a road for the Lord in his mind as far as Kānāi Nāṭaśālā (Madhya 1.155-162), and brought the Lord in meditation to Śivānanda Sena's house to eat his cooking (Antya 2). The record «Pradyumna Brahmacārī» #1097 was the same person and was joined to this one (07-11-2026); its text also told of Nakula Brahmacārī's āveśa at Ambikā (his own record).

fields.aka: Kāśīśvara, Kāśīśvara Paṇḍit, Kāśīśvara Paṇḍita Gosvāmī, Kāśīśvara Gosāñi, Kāśīnātha Paṇḍita (of Cātarā)
fields.disappearance: Kārtika śukla caturdaśī (Gauḍīya calendar; one text: Āśvina pūrṇimā); 1486 Śaka (1564 AD), on the Caitrī Vāruṇī, in Vṛndāvana (Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna, «Kāśīnātha Paṇḍita»)
fields.place: Born at Brāhmaṇaḍāṅgā (Jessore); Cātarā, near Śrīrāmpur (Gaurāṅgapur, his Gaura-Nitāi); Purī; Vṛndāvana (Śrī Gaura-Govinda beside Govindadeva)
fields.disciples: Govinda Gosāñi (pūjārī of Śrī Govinda, Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 8.66); Murāri, son of his brother Mahādeva Bhaṭṭācārya

fields.name: Bijalī Khān
fields.aka: Pathan Vaiṣṇava Bijali Khan, Bijulī Khān
fields.notes: A young Pathān prince who met the Lord on the road from Vṛndāvana to Prayāga, with his soldiers and their learned teacher (named Rāmadāsa by the Lord); all became Vaiṣṇavas, the «Pathān Vaiṣṇavas», and Bijalī Khān a mahā-bhāgavata honoured at all the holy places (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Madhya 18.161-212; Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna).

In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Kṣīrodakaśāyī Viṣṇu, an expansion of Saṅkarṣaṇa (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 67).

Son of Śrī Nityānanda and Vasudhā; sister Gaṅgā Devī; disciple of Jāhnavā Mātā. «After Nityānanda the greatest branch» (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 11.8-12). Married Śrīmatī and Nārāyaṇī, daughters of Yadunandana Ācārya of Jhāmaṭapura (Bhakti-ratnākara 13). Sons and disciples: Gopījana-vallabha (Latā), Rāmakṛṣṇa (Gaṇeśapura, Māldaha), Rāmacandra (Khaḍadaha); daughter Bhuvanamohinī. Went to Vṛndāvana; organised the Vaiṣṇavas of Bengal; excommunicated Jayagopāla dāsa; forbade the cūḍā (the Cūḍādhārīs).

In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Kṣīrodakaśāyī (Payodhiśāyī) Viṣṇu, an expansion of Saṅkarṣaṇa; also Niśaṭha and Ulmuka (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 67).

The record «Birchandra Prabhu» #157 was the same person and was joined to this one (07-11-2026).

fields.appearance: About 1453 Śaka, 1531 AD (Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna); 1452 Śaka, 1530 AD (Digdarśanī)
fields.disappearance: Pauṣa pūrṇimā (his festival at Kāndaḍā: the record's text, Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna)
fields.place: Kāndaḍā (Kāndrā), near Katwa (Bardhamān): birthplace and his maṭha
fields.works: Padas in Bengali and Vrajabuli (pūrva-rāga, sakhī-śikṣā, milana, naukā-khaṇḍa, muralī-śikṣā, goṣṭha-vihāra, māna, māthura, praśna-dūtikā)
fields.notes: A famous padakartā and musician of Nityānanda's branch, disciple of Jāhnavā Devī (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 11.52). He spread the bhuvana-maṅgala harināma in his village and was called Maṅgala Ṭhākura; never married; Bābā Āula Manohara dāsa was his companion (Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna).

name: Yadunandana Dāsa (disciple of Hemalatā, author of the Karṇānanda)

fields.name: Acyutānanda dāsa (Pañcasakhā)
fields.place: Born at Tilkaṇā, near Nembālā (Cuttack, Orissa); Purī
fields.works: Śūnya-saṁhitā, Śabda-brahmāṇḍa-saṁhitā, Anākāra-saṁhitā, Mahā-nitya-rahasa, Nitya-rahasa, Śūnya-rahasa, Vṛnda-rasa, Rādhā-rasa, Bhaviṣya-mālikā
fields.notes: One of the Pañcasakhās, the five Oriyā companions of Lord Caitanya at Purī; son of Dīnabandhu Khuṇṭiyā and Padmāvatī. The Lord (or, by the Śūnya-saṁhitā, Sanātana of Doligrāma on His order) gave him Harināma; he led a saṅkīrtana party and wrote a vast number of works (Bhakti Movement in Orissa pp. 73-75). In the Śūnya-saṁhitā: Sudāmā in Kṛṣṇa-līlā.

fields.name: Rūpacandra Sarasvatī
fields.aka: Rupacandra Sarasvatī, Rūpanārāyaṇa (the name Narottama gave him)
fields.place: Born at Viṭādiyā (Bhiṭādiyā) near Egārasindura (Kāmarūpa, Assam); court paṇḍita of King Narasiṁha at Pakkapallī; Egārasindura (Śrī Rādhā-Vrajamohana)
fields.notes: A great scholar of Assam (titles Cakravartī, Ācārya, Sarasvatī, Mahā-śrutidhara), defeated by Jīva Gosvāmī in Vṛndāvana; sent by King Narasiṁha to defeat Narottama, he took dīkṣā from him with the King and Queen and was named Rūpanārāyaṇa (Prema-vilāsa). Not Rūpanārāyaṇa Cakravartī of Kheturī (#1332).

fields.guru: Hṛdayānanda, of Gaurīdāsa's line (Dibākara dāsa); the Lord gave him the Rāma-tāraka mantra (Īśvara dāsa)
fields.works: Jagamohana Rāmāyaṇa; Vedānta-sāra-gupta-gītā; Bhagavad-gītā (Oriyā); Brahma-purāṇa, Kānta Koili, Gupta-gītā, Bāṭa Abakāśa, Bhāva-samudra, Amarakoṣa-gītā, Brahmāṇḍa-bhūgola, Saptāṅga-yoga-sāra-gītā, Bhāgavata-ṭīkā, Beda-parikramā, Arjuna-gītā
fields.notes:
The eldest of the Pañcasakhās of Orissa, a great devotee of Jagannātha; son of Somanātha Mahāpātra and Mānamāyā. The Lord called him Subala and gave him the Rāma-tāraka mantra; he tamed a mad elephant of Pratāparudra with the holy name and the Lord called him «Matta»; the King honoured him as Paramaguru. He initiated Jagannātha dāsa at the Lord's request (Bhakti Movement in Orissa, citing Īśvara dāsa and Dibākara dāsa).

The record also held six other Balarāmas, now in their own records (07-11-2026).
